page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr6.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on external block storage and network-attached resources. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.hfr6.8xlarge demonstrates solid mid-range performance. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1436.69 and a multi-core score of 30656.07. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1704.61 GB/sec, which drops to 112.52 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 49.63 GB/sec. Database operations are supported by a Redis SET throughput of 28.86 million operations per second and a Passmark database score of 11530.5. For lightweight AI workloads, the instance processes 1572.28 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model, though performance scales down to 46.27 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfr6.8xlarge offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable compute performance, while the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides high resource density for in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications. This hardware configuration is highly suited for running Redis deployments, medium-scale relational databases, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory overhead without the premium cost of local SSDs.
